Defects and surfaces can introduce states within the ideal bulk gap.

records.claim_scope: In the ideal diffusion model, $I=I_S\left(e^{qV/(k_BT)}-1\right)$: current $I$, reverse saturation current $I_S$, junction voltage $V$, elementary charge $q$, absolute temperature $T$ and Boltzmann constant $k_B$. See del Alamo, MIT 6.012, [lecture 14](https://web.mit.edu/6.012/www/SP07-L14.pdf) (2007), pp. 13–16. This is a model with a range of validity, not an exact law for every diode; recombination, series resistance, high injection and breakdown require further treatment.

records.claim_scope: Rolf Landauer, [“Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process”](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.53.0183), *IBM Journal of Research and Development* 5 (1961): 183–191; Charles H. Bennett, [“Notes on Landauer's Principle, Reversible Computation, and Maxwell's Demon”](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0210005), *Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics* 34 (2003): 501–510. For ideal reset of an initially unknown, equally probable binary memory coupled to a thermal reservoir at temperature $T$, the familiar lower bound on average heat delivered to the reservoir is $Q\geq k_BT\ln 2$. Known or correlated bits and other physical arrangements require their information and entropy balances to be specified. This is not a universal cost of every act of forgetting, a claim that storage is free, or a proof that memory promotes growth.
records.evidence_scope: Landauer publisher metadata checked; Bennett abstract and opening PDF pp. 1–2 inspected during comparison. Conditions and logical/physical distinction checked; not a full new reading of Landauer 1961.
